highlights.title: No account required
highlights.description: The app opens without sign-in. Connecting a model provider is what needs credentials, and you choose which one.

highlights.title: Your data stays local
highlights.description: Conversations, artifacts and settings live in a folder on your machine. Export everything or wipe it in two clicks.

highlights.title: Plan before it writes
highlights.description: Plan mode disables edits. The agent reads the project, returns the steps and waits for your approval.

Features.title: A workspace, not a chat box
Features.subtitle: Three modes, one place. Everything the agent does is visible before, during and after it happens.

localFirst.title: Your data stays local
localFirst.description: Conversations, artifacts and settings live in a folder on your machine. Export everything or wipe it in two clicks.

planMode.title: Plan before it writes
planMode.description: Plan mode disables edits and turns your request into steps you can read, approve or send back for another round.

permissions.title: Permission by risk
permissions.description: Read, Review, Edit and Autonomous. Every command is labelled by risk — read, command, destructive, secret or outside the workspace — before it runs.

diffs.title: Read the diff, not the promise
diffs.description: Changes open in a side panel per file or per turn. Revert one file, revert the whole turn, or commit what survived your review.

skills.title: Skills and project context
skills.description: Reusable skills, a custom system prompt and per-tool switches keep the agent aligned with how your project actually works.

modes.title: Chat, Code and Agents
modes.description: A conversation, a coding session or a team of personas — the same session can move between modes without losing its history.

Workflow.title: Plan, run, verify — and stop at any step
Workflow.subtitle: Each step leaves evidence. Nothing is hidden behind a spinner.

steps.title: Plan
steps.description: Describe the task and turn on Plan mode. The agent reads the project and returns the steps it intends to take — no file is touched.
steps.detail: Approve, keep planning, or edit the plan. The composer stays locked until you decide.

steps.title: Execute
steps.description: Pick a permission mode. The agent reads, edits and runs commands inside the workspace, and asks before anything risky.
steps.detail: A running turn shows its steps, its token usage and a stop button that actually stops it.

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: Every edit arrives as a diff. Run the tests, read the changes, revert what you dislike and commit what is left.
steps.detail: The session keeps the model that produced each answer, so the history stays honest.

Positioning.title: Built for people who read the diff
Positioning.subtitle: Zylara is opinionated in one direction: you should be able to see what the agent is about to do, and stop it.

points.title: Nothing runs silently
points.description: A command, an edit or a deletion is a request. Risk is shown, approval is explicit, and a denial is a normal answer — not an error.

points.title: One session, three views
points.description: A chat that became a coding session is still the same conversation. Switch modes and keep the transcript, the model and the context.

points.title: Your machine, your rules
points.description: There is no workspace in the cloud to sync. The app reads the folders you open and writes only where you allow it.

Positioning.limitsSubtitle: Limits stated up front, so you do not find them after installing.

limits.title: No cloud sync
limits.description: There is no hosted workspace. To use it on another machine you take the data folder with you.

limits.title: It does not pick the model
limits.description: You connect a provider and pay usage directly to it. The app does not resell tokens.

limits.title: No mobile or web app yet
limits.description: Chat, Code and Agents run on the desktop. Windows is the stable build; macOS and Linux are in beta.

limits.title: It does not replace review
limits.description: The agent can be wrong. Plan, permissions and diffs exist so you check before accepting.

Faq.title: Frequently asked

items.question: Where does my data go?
items.answer: Conversations, artifacts and settings live in a local folder on your computer. Only the messages you send reach the model provider you configured, and you can export or delete the whole data folder at any time.

items.question: How much does Zylara cost?
items.answer: The app is free, open source under MIT, and opens without an account. What costs money is the model: you pay the provider directly — subscription, credits or API key. The app does not resell tokens.

items.question: Which models can I use?
items.answer: OpenCode Go, OpenCode Zen, OpenAI through a ChatGPT plan and Anthropic with an API key. In Code and Agents you can switch models between turns; earlier answers keep the model that produced them.

items.question: What exactly is Plan mode?
items.answer: A mode where edits are off. The agent reads the project, writes a plan and waits. You can approve, keep planning or go back to the session. A plan badge in the composer shows when the mode is on.

items.question: Can the agent run commands on its own?
items.answer: Only as far as the permission mode allows. Read, Review, Edit and Autopilot define how much it can do without asking, and risky actions stay labelled and exposed for approval.

items.question: Why are macOS and Linux beta?
items.answer: Windows is the stable target: it gets the installers, the auto-update flow and the testing. macOS and Linux builds exist so you can try them and report problems — expect rough edges between versions.

items.question: How does Zylara compare to other coding agents?
items.answer: We do not claim to be faster. The difference is where the work happens: a desktop app with local data, a plan before any edit, and permissions labelled by risk. If you want the agent inside your editor or fully in the cloud, there are good tools for that too.

items.question: Does it work offline?
items.answer: The app and its data are local, so browsing conversations, artifacts and skills works without a connection. Generating answers requires the provider you chose to be reachable.

items.question: What are the system requirements?
items.answer: Windows 10/11 x64 is the stable build. macOS on Apple Silicon and Linux x64 (AppImage, .deb and .rpm) are experimental. The app is built with Tauri, so it uses the system webview instead of bundling a browser.

items.question: Is the source code open?
items.answer: Yes: MIT, at Hyska-Software/ZylaraAi. You can read, build and redistribute it; builds cannot use the name or logo in a way that suggests an official release.

items.question: How do I delete my data?
items.answer: Conversations, artifacts and settings live in a folder in your user profile. Delete that folder, or uninstall the app and remove it — we never had a copy to delete.

items.question: Can I run more than one chat at a time?
items.answer: Yes: chats, code sessions and agent teams sit side by side in the sidebar, and each one keeps its own transcript, model and context.

sections.title: Who we are and what these terms cover
body: Zylara is a desktop application published by Hyska Software. The source code is available in the project repository under the MIT licence, and for the code itself the licence prevails over these terms.
These terms cover downloading and running the builds we publish, and using this website. They do not cover the services you connect to from the app, which have their own terms.

sections.title: What stays on your machine
body: Zylara is local-first: conversations, artifacts, skills, settings and the credentials of the providers you connect are written to a data folder in your user profile. There is no cloud workspace to sync.
Removing the app and deleting that folder removes the content. Backups are your responsibility — we cannot recover a folder we never had.
items: Folders you open are read and written only within the permissions you grant.
Commands run through your own shell, with your own user account.

sections.title: Accounts and model providers
body: The app opens without an account. Signing in is only needed to reach a model: OpenCode Go, OpenCode Zen, OpenAI through a ChatGPT plan or an API key, and Anthropic through an API key.

Usage and billing belong to the provider you choose. When you connect an account with your own credentials, that provider processes your prompts under its own terms and privacy policy; we act only as the client on your machine.

sections.title: Acceptable use
body: Use Zylara only for work you are allowed to do, in code and projects you are allowed to change.
items: Do not use the app to break the law, to infringe copyright or to attack systems you do not own.
Do not redistribute builds under a name, logo or signature that suggests an official release.
Do not try to obtain credentials or data that belong to someone else.

sections.title: Model output is not guaranteed
body: Language models produce plausible text, not verified facts. Plans, edits, commands and summaries can be incomplete or wrong.
Plan mode, permission modes and diffs exist so you can check the work before it lands. Reviewing what the agent wrote before accepting it is part of using the app.

sections.title: Downloads, updates and availability
body: Installers are published for Windows, macOS and Linux, and every download can be checked against the published SHA-256 checksums.

The app updates only when you install a new version; nothing is installed silently. Features may change between versions, and we may stop publishing a platform build — the source stays available under the MIT licence.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
body: When the text changes, the revision date at the top changes with it. Continuing to use the site or the app after a revision means accepting the new version; if you disagree, stop using the app and delete the data folder.
Material changes are also announced in the release notes of the version where they take effect.

PrivacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPage.subtitle: What Zylara stores on your computer, what actually reaches us, and what you can ask us to do with it — region by region.
summary: Conversations, artifacts, files and API keys stay in the data folder on your machine.
No analytics, advertising or third-party trackers on this site. The only cookie remembers your language.
Prompts go only to the model provider you configured, under that provider's own policy.

sections.title: Who is responsible
body: Hyska Software is the controller of the personal data described here. Every request goes to legal@hyska.com.br.
This policy covers this website and the Zylara desktop app. Services you connect to from the app are covered by their own policies.

sections.title: What stays on your machine
body: Conversations, artifacts, skills, settings, saved tokens and the record of a session are stored in the app's data folder, in your user profile. They are not uploaded to us and we cannot read them.

Deleting that folder erases the content. Files you export go wherever you saved them, outside our reach. Protecting the folder is a matter of your operating system and, if you need it, of disk encryption.

sections.title: What reaches us
body: We receive only what you choose to send: an e-mail to legal@hyska.com.br, or a public issue or pull request in the repository, which carries your GitHub username.

The servers that deliver this website keep technical access records — IP address, user agent, requested page and time — used to keep the site available and to detect abuse. They are not combined with any other information about you.

sections.title: Model providers
body: Generating a response means sending the prompt, the context you attached and the resulting output to the provider you selected: OpenCode Go, OpenCode Zen, OpenAI (ChatGPT plan or API key) or Anthropic (API key).

In that exchange the provider processes the content under its own privacy policy and, when you use your own account, as an independent controller. Your keys and tokens are stored locally and are not sent to us.
Content sent to a provider may be stored or reviewed by it according to its policy and your account settings. Read them before pasting credentials, personal data or third-party code.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
body: This site sets a single cookie, NEXT_LOCALE, which stores the language you picked so the next visit opens in it. It lasts up to one year and can be removed by clearing site data in your browser.
There is no analytics, no advertising pixel and no third-party tracker. If that changes, this policy is updated first and consent is requested where the law requires it.

sections.title: Security
body: Your conversations never pass through a storage service of ours, which removes the most common cause of leaks. What remains is your device and the provider you chose.
No system is perfect. If you find a vulnerability, report it privately through the repository's security channel instead of opening a public issue.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
body: When this policy changes, the revision date at the top changes with it, and material changes are announced on this page before they take effect.
Earlier versions stay in the repository history, so you can compare what changed.

unitedStates.title: For users in the United States
unitedStates.intro: This section applies to residents of the United States, including California, and describes the categories of personal information we handle under state privacy laws.

sections.title: Scope
body: This section covers the processing described in this policy when you are a resident of a US state with a comprehensive privacy law, such as the CCPA as amended by the CPRA.

sections.title: What we collect
body: Identifiers: IP address and e-mail address, when you write to us. Internet activity: pages requested and the time of the request, in server logs. Account data: the GitHub username attached to a public issue.
We do not collect sensitive personal information, precise geolocation, biometric data or commercial information such as purchase history — there is no purchase today.

sections.title: Why we collect it
body: To answer your message, to keep the site available and secure, to investigate abuse and to comply with legal obligations. We do not use it for profiling or targeted advertising.

sections.title: Sale and sharing
body: We do not sell personal information, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising as those terms are defined by the CPRA. Global Privacy Control signals are honoured as an opt-out of sale and sharing.
Providers that host the site process requests on our instruction and are bound to use them only for that purpose.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can ask what we hold about you, request a copy, ask us to correct or delete it, and ask for the categories shared. Exercising a right never changes the service you get.
Write to legal@hyska.com.br with the subject “privacy request”, or use an authorised agent. We confirm receipt within 10 business days and answer within 45 days, extended where the law allows.

sections.title: Children
body: The app is not directed to children under 13 and we do not knowingly collect their personal information. If you believe a child sent us data, write to us and we delete it.

europe.title: For users in Europe
europe.intro: This section applies to data subjects in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland and describes the processing under the GDPR.

sections.title: Scope
body: This section covers the processing described in this policy when you are in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland. Where national law adds requirements, those requirements apply on top of it.

sections.title: Legal bases
body: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR — to answer a request you sent about the app or a download. Art. 6(1)(f) — legitimate interest in keeping the site available, secure and free of abuse, limited to technical logs. Art. 6(1)(c) — compliance with a legal obligation. Art. 6(1)(a) — consent, when we ask for it explicitly.

sections.title: Retention
body: Data is kept only as long as the purpose requires: server logs for the short period needed to detect and investigate abuse, and correspondence for the time needed to answer it plus the applicable limitation period.
When that period ends, records are deleted or anonymised.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You have the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection (Art. 15 to 21 GDPR), and the right to withdraw consent at any time without affecting processing already carried out.

We answer without undue delay and within one month, extendable by two months for complex requests with notice. Requests are free, may be made through a representative, and the answer can be requested in a machine-readable format.

sections.title: International transfers
body: Some providers involved may process data outside the EEA: the model provider you connect to, and the infrastructure that serves this site. Transfers rely on an adequacy decision or on the Standard Contractual Clauses of 2021/914, and you can ask for details.
Local-first is the default: the app sends nothing anywhere until you start a turn.

sections.title: Complaints and children
body: You may complain to the supervisory authority of the country where you live, work or where the alleged infringement occurred, after giving us the chance to answer first.
The data protection age is 16 in the EU, unless a member state set it lower, never below 13 (Art. 8 GDPR). Do not use the app below that age.

brazil.title: For data subjects in Brazil
brazil.intro: This section applies to data subjects in Brazil and describes the processing carried out under the LGPD (Law 13.709/2018).

sections.title: Scope and roles
body: Hyska Software is the controller of the data described in this policy. When you connect your own account at a model provider, that provider processes the content as an independent controller under its own policy.
The Brazilian Data Protection Authority (ANPD) is the competent authority in Brazil.

sections.title: Legal bases
body: Consent (art. 7, I) to answer your message; legitimate interest (art. 7, IX) in keeping the site available and secure, limited to technical logs; compliance with a legal obligation (art. 7, II); and performance of a contract (art. 7, V), where one exists.

sections.title: Rights of the data subject
body: You can ask for confirmation that we process your data, and for access, correction, anonymisation, blocking or deletion of unnecessary data, portability, deletion of data processed with consent, information about sharing and review of automated decisions (arts. 18 and 20 of the LGPD).
Requests are free of charge and can be made at legal@hyska.com.br. We answer within the 15 days set by art. 19 of the LGPD.

sections.title: Retention and international transfers
body: Data is kept for as long as the purpose requires and is then deleted or anonymised.

Model and infrastructure providers may process data outside Brazil. In those cases we apply art. 33 of the LGPD — specific contractual clauses, binding corporate rules or another legal basis — and you can ask for information about the transfer.

sections.title: Data protection officer
body: The channel of the data protection officer (encarregado) is legal@hyska.com.br, for requests from data subjects and communications with the ANPD.

sections.title: Children and adolescents
body: The app is not directed to children. Data of children under 12 is processed only with the specific consent of a parent or legal guardian, under art. 14 of the LGPD, and always in their best interest.

contact.title: How to exercise your rights
body: Write to legal@hyska.com.br with the right you want to exercise and the e-mail address involved. We answer in the period set for your region and never charge for it.

WhyZylaraPage.metaDescription: Local-first, a plan before the edit, risk-based permissions and a reviewable diff. Zylara's choices, its limits stated plainly and who the app is — and is not — for.
WhyZylaraPage.title: Built for people who read the diff
WhyZylaraPage.subtitle: Zylara is opinionated in one direction: you need to see what the agent is about to do, and be able to stop it. The rest follows.

principles.title: Four choices that explain the rest
principles.subtitle: None of them is an isolated feature; all of them show up in the same turn.

items.title: Nothing runs silently
items.description: A command, an edit or a deletion is a request. Risk shows up, approval is explicit and denying is a normal answer.

items.title: Evidence before the promise
items.description: Plan, diff and result stay in the transcript. The session does not ask for trust: it shows what it did, in what order and with which model.

items.title: Reversible by default
items.description: Reverting a file or a whole turn is a first-class action, not an undo hidden in a menu.

items.title: Data where the work happens
items.description: The data folder lives on your machine. There is no hosted workspace to sync and no copy of ours to leak.

compare.title: Where the work happens
compare.subtitle: Three categories of tool, not three products. Compare by what you can check, not by what the demo shows.

The folder open in the editor

cells: Panel per file and per turn

compare.note: Categories change fast and every vendor has its own documentation. The Zylara column describes this version of the app; check the release notes for what changed.

localFirst.title: What staying local costs
localFirst.subtitle: Local-first is not a security badge. It is a trade — and it comes with duties on your side.

items.title: No sync
items.description: There is no hosted workspace. Using another machine means copying the data folder — and keeping both in sync is on you.

items.title: Backup is yours
items.description: We have no copy of your conversations to restore. A disk backup solves it; we cannot solve it for you.

items.title: Requires a provider
items.description: The app works offline to browse what already exists. Generating a reply requires the provider you connected to be reachable.

items.title: One machine at a time
items.description: There is no multi-device presence, concurrent editing or shared history between people.

limits.title: What Zylara does not do
limits.subtitle: Said plainly, so you do not find out after installing.

items.title: It is not an IDE
items.description: It does not replace your editor, LSP or debugger. Zylara opens the folder and works in it; the editor stays the editor.

items.title: It does not host a model
items.description: No model runs inside the app. Without a connected provider, there is no reply.

items.title: It does not sync or collaborate
items.description: There is no shared workspace, team comments or live session for someone else to join.

items.title: It does not replace review
items.description: Plan, permissions and diff reduce risk; they do not guarantee the change compiles, passes tests or is correct.

items.title: It has no web or mobile app
items.description: Chat, Code and Agents run on desktop. Windows is the stable build; macOS and Linux are in beta.

items.title: It installs nothing silently
items.description: Updates only land when you install a new version. The notice exists; the click is yours.

audience.title: Who it is for — and who it is not
audience.subtitle: The app does not try to serve everyone. Recognizing yourself in both lists is part of choosing well.
forItems: You already use a coding agent and want to see what it runs
You work in a private repository and prefer the data on your machine
You need a reviewable plan before any edit
You switch models by task and cost
notForItems: You want the agent inside the editor, with no other window
You want to run a local model without connecting a provider
You need real-time collaboration in a workspace
You want full autonomy without reviewing plan or diff

FaqPage.metaDescription: Data, cost, models, permissions, platforms and license: the complete answers about Zylara, grouped by subject.
FaqPage.title: Frequently asked questions
FaqPage.subtitle: The answers that block a download and the ones that show up later — by subject, without detours.

items.question: How do I connect my own API key?
items.answer: In Settings › Providers. The key is written to the local data folder and used in the calls that leave your machine. Zylara supports OpenCode Go, OpenCode Zen, OpenAI through a ChatGPT plan or API key, and Anthropic through an API key.

items.question: Is there a token limit per turn?
items.answer: The app shows the turn's token usage but imposes no limit of its own: the limit belongs to the provider and plan you connected. When it refuses, the turn ends with the provider error in the transcript.

items.question: Does Zylara resell tokens or charge a markup?
items.answer: No. The app is MIT and does not intermediate billing. The provider charges your account directly, at the price it publishes.

items.question: What happens if I run out of credits?
items.answer: The turn fails with the provider message. The transcript, artifacts and settings stay local; you switch routes, adjust the plan and continue the same conversation.

items.question: What does the risk label change in practice?
items.answer: It decides whether the call runs directly or waits for approval. Read, command, destructive, secret and outside the workspace are evaluated before execution, and each one shows up in the transcript with its result.

items.question: What counts as a path outside the workspace?
items.answer: Any path that is not inside the folders you opened. Even in Autopilot, touching those paths asks for approval.

items.question: Does denying a permission break the task?
items.answer: No. Denying is a normal answer: the agent receives the result, adjusts the path and proposes another approach, or hands the plan back for you to review.

items.question: Do my credentials show up in the transcript?
items.answer: Keys stay in the data folder and are not written to the transcript. Still, whatever you paste into the chat goes to the provider: avoid secrets in the prompt.

items.question: How do I know the download is intact?
items.answer: Compare the file's SHA-256 with the SHA256SUMS.txt published alongside the release. The checksums are on the download page and in every release's notes.

items.question: How do I update the app?
items.answer: The app notifies you when a newer stable release exists. Installation is never silent: on Windows it opens the installer, on macOS the DMG and on Linux the package or AppImage.

items.question: Does it run on Windows ARM or Intel macOS?
items.answer: The published builds are Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon and Linux x64. Other architectures require building from source, with no guarantee that everything works.

items.question: Do I need Node.js or Rust to use the app?
items.answer: No. The installers are self-contained and use the system webview. Node.js, Rust and the build tooling only come in if you build from the repository.

items.question: Can I use Zylara at work?
items.answer: Yes. The MIT license allows commercial use, modification and redistribution. The data stays in the local folder of the machine where the app runs.

items.question: Can I publish a fork?
items.answer: You can, under the MIT license. The only practical restriction is the name and logo: a fork should not suggest it is an official build.

items.question: Where do I report a bug or a vulnerability?
items.answer: Bugs and suggestions go to the repository's public issues. Vulnerabilities follow the repository's private security channel, with no details in a public issue.

items.question: Does the site use analytics?
items.answer: There is no analytics, advertising pixel or third-party tracker. The only cookie stores the chosen language, and the details are in the Privacy Policy.
